evidence: Measured in 4 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.05–0.14% of total volatiles (0.01–0.028mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Humulene epoxide II is a monocyclic sesquiterpene, an oxygenated derivative of the common plant aromatic humulene. It contributes to the complex, earthy, and slightly woody aromas found in certain herbs and spices. You might encounter it in the scent of fresh ginger varieties or the distinct fragrance of cannabis leaves.
consumer_summary.found_in: This compound is naturally produced by Cannabis sativa and several members of the ginger family, including grains of paradise (Aframomum melegueta) and shampoo ginger (Zingiber zerumbet).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to humulene epoxide II because it frequently appears in the essential oils of plants with long histories of traditional use. They are actively exploring its potential to act as an anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial agent, as well as its ability to influence cell proliferation. The strongest evidence so far comes from human observational studies (Oxford level 2b) that examine the effects of botanical extracts rich in this terpene. If these properties hold up in isolated testing, it could offer new plant-derived options for managing inflammation and bacterial growth.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether humulene epoxide II can influence tumor cell proliferation and act as a plant-derived antineoplastic agent.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind clinical trial in patients with specific solid tumors, measuring tumor size and relevant biomarkers over 6 to 12 months alongside standard care.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward this molecule acting as a natural insect repellent, which would offer a botanical alternative to synthetic bug sprays.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A human topical application trial measuring mosquito landing rates and bite prevention duration compared to a standard like DEET over an 8-hour period.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: If early findings bear out, this terpene might help modulate pain signaling pathways.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial measuring self-reported pain scores (using a Visual Analog Scale) in participants experiencing acute mild pain over a 24-hour period.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b); most of the rest is animal and lab research on plant extracts.
